request.spec:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The consolidated figures now apply the trim once over the whole tree and count each person once. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The change is entirely in the front end, in `src/main/frontend/features/counters/ConsolidatedFigures.tsx`. No server or stored data needed to change.

- **Due-total and overdue-total:** each sheet now passes up every person's own due and overdue figure instead of its already-trimmed total. Those figures are combined across the tree and trimmed once with the existing `trimmedTotal`: the single highest and single lowest are dropped when three or more people have a figure, and n/a figures are left out.
- **People count:** each sheet now passes up every person's name and aliases, compared the same way the app already compares names (spaces trimmed, case ignored). Two people are counted as one if any of their names or aliases match, and that carries through chains: if A matches B and B matches C, all three count as one.
- **Aliases:** the sheet's aliases are now loaded for the current sheet and for each sheet below it, alongside the people, claims and rates.

One small knock-on change: in `HeaderCounters.tsx`, the name-comparison helper `nameKey` is now exported so the consolidated count uses exactly the same matching as the header.

The per-grade due-totals and per-status counts still add up across sheets as before.

Retired people are still included in the people count and the trim, as they were before.
